## Natural history notes

A large trap-jaw ant characterized by a dark reddish-brown to brown body, long legs, and powerful straight mandibles that can snap shut extremely quickly. In Florida, the Florida Trap-jaw Ant is found in pine flatwoods, hammocks, forest edges, yards, leaf litter, rotting wood, and soil cavities, especially in warm humid habitats with abundant ground cover. Workers hunt small insects and other arthropods, scavenge dead material, and may also take sugary resources, using their spring-loaded jaws for prey capture, defense, and quick escape movements.
